screening_results.reason: Although this study includes VBM analyses (I3), clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants (I4) with adequate group size (n=48; I5), and reports group-level whole-brain VBM results (I7) described in text/figures (I8), it does not present a whole-brain between-group imaging contrast that directly compares the bvFTD group to healthy controls. The reported VBM contrasts are primarily AD versus bvFTD (patient vs patient), and the imaging cohort lacks a concurrent healthy control imaging comparison for bvFTD. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 (bvFTD vs controls imaging contrast in MNI/Talairach space) is not met, so the study must be excluded.

The study uses whole-brain VBM (I3), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD subgroup (n=16) (I4), and has sufficient sample sizes for patient and control groups (I5). However, it does not report any between-group voxelwise contrast (bvFTD vs. healthy controls) in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) specific to the bvFTD group. The VBM analyses reported are brain–behavior correlations across the entire mixed diagnostic sample and co-atrophy-adjusted maps, not group-level bvFTD vs. control contrasts; no bvFTD-specific whole-brain voxelwise results are presented in the main text (I6 and I7 not met). Therefore it fails the requirement for a group-level between-group whole-brain result for the target sample. No exclusion criteria from the list are met. Full text appears complete.

Exclusion criteria met: E6. This study used VBM (I3 satisfied) and included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4 satisfied) with sufficient sample sizes (bvFTD n=13; controls n=20; I5 satisfied). However, the VBM analyses reported in the paper are correlations within the combined patient cohort and significant findings are reported only within pre-specified regional volumes of interest (ROI-level, FWE-corrected within ROIs). The paper does not report any between-group voxelwise contrast in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) comparing the bvFTD group alone versus controls, nor any whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results attributable to the bvFTD group (I6 and I7 not met). Therefore it meets exclusion E6 (only ROI results/no qualifying whole-brain between-group voxelwise result). Full text appears complete and sufficient for assessment (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study meets all required inclusion criteria: it performed a voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analysis (I3) and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=22) according to consensus criteria (I4) with adequate sample sizes for patient and control groups (bvFTD n=22; controls n=34) meeting the >=6 requirement (I5). The VBM was conducted in standard space (registration to MNI template) and patient-control voxelwise comparisons were reported (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results with TFCE and permutation testing), with bvFTD vs. controls contrasts described and results provided in supplementary figures (I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria apply (no review/meta-analysis, not ROI-only, empirical data, not limited to excluded modalities). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, and acknowledgements present).

Exclusion reason: E6 applies — the study reports ROI-based structural MRI volume analyses (summed frontotemporal atlas regions) and does not report whole-brain, voxelwise results in stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). Inclusion met: I5 (patient and control groups both >6 participants: 105 carriers, 69 noncarriers). Inclusions not met: I3 (imaging modality is not VBM, task/resting‑state fMRI, or FDG‑PET as required), I4 (sample is autosomal dominant FTLD mutation carriers, not a clinically-diagnosed bvFTD/Pick’s disease group as specified), I6 (no between-group contrast reported in stereotactic coordinates comparing a bvFTD group to controls), and I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete. Therefore the paper is excluded.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria: it uses resting-state fMRI (I3), includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD patient group (n=21) and matched controls (I4, I5), and reports voxelwise between-group contrasts (two-sample t tests) comparing bvFTD to controls assessed in standard space (MNI coordinates used for seeds and voxelwise analyses) with whole-brain, cluster-level corrected results (satisfying I6 and I7). Results are presented in figures and described in text (acceptable per I8). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the article appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (no review/meta-analysis, not ROI-only, no disallowed comorbid sample, empirical original data, and not limited solely to excluded modalities). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the review.

The study uses VBM and includes adequate sample sizes, but it does not specifically investigate or report results for behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) as a distinct group. The FTD sample is heterogeneous (15 PPA variants; 14 with social/executive dysfunction) and all analyses are reported for the pooled FTD group versus controls; no bvFTD-only between-group voxelwise contrasts or coordinates are provided. Therefore it fails the requirement for inclusion of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients analyzed separately and fails the requirement for bvFTD-specific between-group whole-brain contrasts. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM used), I5 (sample sizes ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (bvFTD-specific sample), I6 (bvFTD vs control contrast not reported), I7 (bvFTD-specific whole-brain result not provided). No exclusion criteria from the list (E5–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

Excluded because the study uses T1-weighted volumetric segmentation of amygdala subnuclei (ROI-based structural volumetry), not one of the required imaging modalities (VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET), and it does not report whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results or stereotactic coordinates. Therefore exclusion criterion E6 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results) applies. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (includes Pick's disease patients among pathological groups) and I5 (patient and control groups both exceed 6 participants). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (imaging modality is not VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET), I6 (no between-group contrasts reported in MNI/Talairach stereotactic space comparing bvFTD to controls), and I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level results reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3), includes clinically diagnosed behavioral variant FTD/FTLD patients (I4), has sufficient sample sizes (7 FTLD with stereotypies, 10 FTLD without, and matched controls) meeting the >=6 requirement (I5), reports voxelwise between-group contrasts in MNI stereotactic space comparing the bvFTD/FTLD groups to controls (I6) using whole-brain VBM analyses (I7), and the whole-brain results are described in the text/figures (I8). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext complete). No exclusion criteria apply (e.g., not a review, not ROI-only, no disallowed modalities or comorbid-sample issues). Note: sample is modest and some secondary analyses used uncorrected thresholds, but these caveats do not violate inclusion/exclusion rules.

This study meets inclusion criteria I3 (uses VBM), I4 (includes a clinically diagnosed bv-FTD group of n=15), and I5 (bvFTD n=15 and controls n=15). However, it does NOT report any whole-brain, voxelwise between-group contrast directly comparing the bvFTD group to controls in a standardized stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). The reported VBM analyses are (a) a comparison of a mixed ‘poor melody score’ patient subgroup (patients with mixed diagnoses) vs controls and (b) covariate/correlation analyses across all patients merged together. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not satisfied (no bvFTD vs control voxelwise contrast reported), so the study cannot be included for the meta-analysis. No exclusion criteria from the provided list are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I6: it does not report a between-group contrast comparing a bvFTD group to healthy controls in MNI/Talairach space. The paper reports within-group VBM regression analyses correlating reward-seeking scores in a bvFTD-only sample (group-level voxelwise results), not a bvFTD vs control whole-brain comparison. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses voxel-based morphometry), I4 (sample comprises clinically diagnosed behavioural variant FTD patients), I5 (patient sample n=91 for imaging analyses, ≥6), I7 (reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results from the target bvFTD sample), I8 (results reported in MNI coordinates). Exclusion criteria met: none. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study meets all required inclusion criteria for the review. It used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as the imaging modality (I3). The sample includes a clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bv-FTD) subgroup (n=27) (I4) and a healthy control group (n=14), satisfying the minimum group sizes (I5). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise analyses with results in MNI space (coordinates provided for significant clusters) and describes between-group VBM comparisons (each diagnostic group vs controls) referenced in the text and supplementary table (fulfilling I6, I7). Reporting of voxelwise results in the main text and supplementary materials meets the allowance for coordinates/figures/supplements (I8). No exclusion criteria are met: this is an empirical VBM study (not a review), it reports whole-brain results (not ROI-only), and does not rely on excluded modalities. Therefore I include the study.

This is an original empirical study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients using whole-brain voxel-based morphometry and resting-state fMRI (seed-based analyses). The sample includes 87 bvFTD patients (21 with criminal behavior) and 26 healthy controls, meeting sample-size requirements. The paper reports whole-brain, voxel-/vertex-wise results (with MNI normalization and x,y,z coordinates) comparing bvFTD subgroups and bvFTD vs. controls, and provides region-based analyses and figures/tables. Full methods, results, and discussion are present; supplemental material is not required for core outcomes. Although a small subset of patients had histories of alcohol/drug abuse (4/21), the primary sample and contrasts focus on clinically defined bvFTD and report whole-brain results; this does not preclude inclusion given the review criteria. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria relevant to the meta-analysis.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the bvFTD-specific and whole-brain result criteria. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (used VBM/tissue segmentation and VBM8 pipeline) and I5 (FTD patient group N=12 and controls N=18, both ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (FTD cases are reported without distinguishing subtypes — bvFTD or Pick's disease is not explicitly identified), I6 (no reported between-group voxelwise contrasts in MNI/Talairach space comparing a bvFTD-only group to controls), I7 (no clearly identified group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results for a target bvFTD sample). No exclusion criteria from the list were triggered. Full text appears complete and provides methods/results/discussion.

This is an empirical VBM study (FSL-VBM) that includes a clearly defined bvFTD patient group (n=19) and healthy controls (n=25). Sample sizes exceed the minimum (>=6). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses and between-group contrasts versus controls with results provided in stereotactic (MNI) space (clusters and coordinates reported in Table 3 and supplement). It also reports bvFTD-specific whole-brain covariate analyses correlating caloric intake with gray matter atrophy (bvFTD not pooled with other patient groups). Core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present, so full text is complete. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion requirements for the review objective of bvFTD imaging studies.

The study is excluded because, although it uses resting-state fMRI (I3) and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients within a mixed FTD sample (I4), it does NOT meet key inclusion criteria required for this review. The bvFTD subgroup has only 4 participants (<6), failing I5. The paper does not report any between-group, whole-brain voxelwise contrast specifically comparing a bvFTD group to controls (bvFTD is pooled with other FTD subtypes), so I6 and I7 are not satisfied. The full text is complete and no exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Summary: inclusion criteria met: I3, I4; inclusion criteria not met: I5, I6, I7. No exclusion criteria applied.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review. It used FDG-PET imaging (I3) in a sample consisting exclusively of clinically diagnosed behavioral/frontal variant FTD patients (bvFTD) (I4). The overall patient sample (N=142) and PET subgroup (N=41) exceed the minimum required sample size, and healthy comparison groups (N=292 overall comparisons; N=16 for PET) meet the control size threshold (I5). The paper reports voxelwise, whole-brain SPM analyses with results provided in stereotactic coordinates (MNI transformed to Talairach) for group contrasts between bvFTD patients and controls, and between haplotype-defined bvFTD subgroups, not pooled with other disorders (I6, I7). Results are presented as tables/figures with coordinates (I8). The provided full text includes background, methods, results, and discussion; it appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are met. Therefore the study should be included.

This study is excluded because it does not meet key target-sample and result-reporting inclusion criteria. Although it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3) and includes sufficient numbers in the FTD patient group (n=11) and controls (n=22) (I5), the paper does not explicitly identify a clinically-diagnosed behavioral variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick’s disease subgroup (I4 is not clearly met—authors report ‘FTD’ without specifying bvFTD). Crucially, the study does not report a between-group whole-brain (voxelwise) contrast explicitly comparing a bvFTD group to controls (I6 and I7 are not met); the primary VBM results are correlations across a mixed diagnostic sample, not group-level bvFTD vs control voxelwise contrasts. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it reports only region-of-interest measurements (AC and SI thickness/area) from structural 3T MRI and provides no whole-brain voxelwise analyses or coordinate-based between-group contrasts. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (sample includes clinically diagnosed frontotemporal dementia variant within the FTLD subgroup) and I5 (patient group n=7; control group n=16). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (imaging modality is not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET), I6 (no between-group contrasts reported in MNI/Talairach or equivalent coordinate space), I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level results). The full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

The study uses VBM (I3) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group contrasts with MNI-like coordinates for a bvFTD clinical subgroup vs controls (I6, I7). It clearly includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4) and presents whole-brain results in figures/text (I8). However, the paper does not explicitly report the number of bvFTD patients in the bvFTD subgroup in the provided full text (the overall sample is 18 patients but clinical-group counts are not specified in the text available here), so the required minimum patient-group size criterion (I5: ≥6 bvFTD participants) cannot be verified. No exclusion criteria from the review are met. Because a key numeric eligibility item (I5) cannot be confirmed from the provided full text, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

The full text reports voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses (I3) and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=19) (I4) with a healthy control group (n=20) meeting the sample-size requirement (I5). The paper reports voxel-wise, whole-brain two-sample t-tests comparing each patient group (bvFTD and SD) to controls in standard space (MNI) (I6,I7); behavioural VBM correlations are also reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not restricted to non-qualifying modalities, and no comorbid psychiatric/substance confounds reported). Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study is excluded because it does not provide the required between-group whole-brain (voxelwise) contrast comparing a bvFTD group to healthy controls in standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses VBM), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients; n=22), I5 (patient group size ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no reported between-group contrast of bvFTD versus controls in MNI/Talairach space; VBM analyses are within patient cohorts relating symptoms to grey matter, not bvFTD vs controls), I7 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD vs control comparison). No exclusion criteria from the review were triggered (exclusion_criteria_applied = []). The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

Decision: EXCLUDED. Rationale: The study uses FDG-PET imaging and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise comparisons of an FTD group versus controls in Talairach space, with an adequate sample size (FTD n=13; controls n=26). However, the paper does not specify that the FTD sample comprises clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick's disease, and the meta-analysis inclusion criterion I4 explicitly requires bvFTD or Pick's disease. Therefore it fails I4 and must be excluded. (a) Exclusion IDs met: none. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I3 (FDG-PET), I5 (>=6 patients and controls), I6 (between-group voxelwise contrast in Talairach space for the FTD group vs controls), I7 (reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results for the FTD group), I8 (results presented/defined in text/figures). (c) Inclusion IDs NOT met: I4 (clinical diagnosis specifically of bvFTD or Pick's disease not clearly reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

Exclusion reason: E6 (only ROI/ no qualifying whole-brain between-group results). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses VBM, rs-fMRI, and FDG-PET), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients, n=11), I5 (bvFTD group size ≥6). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no reported between-group voxelwise contrast comparing bvFTD to healthy controls; study focuses on classification among patient groups rather than bvFTD vs controls), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise result clearly reported as coming from bvFTD vs controls). The full text appears complete. Therefore excluded because it does not provide the required whole-brain between-group voxelwise results for bvFTD vs controls.

This is an empirical VBM study of bvFTD using whole-brain voxelwise analyses. The paper uses voxel-based morphometry on T1-weighted MRI (preprocessed in CAT12/SPM12, normalized to MNI space), reports group-level VBM contrasts comparing 82 clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients to 80 healthy controls with voxelwise results (FDR/FWE thresholds, cluster tables/figures referenced). Disease staging is specified and bvFTD is not pooled with other patient groups. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (reviews, ROI-only, non-empirical, seed-only FC/DTI/cortical thickness, or comorbid-sample issues) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and is eligible for inclusion.

The study is excluded because it fails inclusion criterion I5 (minimum sample size). Both bvFTD patient groups are N=5 (bvFTD(CBD)=5; bvFTD(Pick’s)=5), below the required >=6. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses VBM), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD / Pick’s patients), I6 (reports between-group contrasts in SPM5 with coordinate-based results), I7 (reports whole-brain voxelwise group results), I8 (reports results in tables/figures described in text). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (patient group sizes <6). Exclusion criteria applicable: none (E5,E6,E7,E8,E9 not met). Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Excluded because imaging methods are surface-based cortical thickness analyses rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET, which triggers exclusion criterion E9. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample; n=88 patients) and I5 (>=6 patients and >=6 controls; 88 patients, 30 controls). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (did not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET), I6 (no between-group contrasts reported in a defined stereotactic coordinate space such as MNI/Talairach — analyses are vertex/surface-based and coordinates/tables in stereotactic space are not provided), and I7 (while whole-brain surface maps are reported, the study does not provide voxelwise whole-brain results in a defined stochastic (MNI/Talairach) space required by the review). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical VBM study of patients clinically diagnosed with frontotemporal dementia (FTD) using Neary criteria; the overeating subgroup comprises 6 FTD patients (target bvFTD-like behavioral phenotype) and imaging analysis included voxel-wise contrasts versus 47 healthy controls and 21 nonovereating patients. The study uses VBM (I3), includes clinically diagnosed FTD/bvFTD patients (I4), has at least 6 patients in the target patient subgroup and sufficient controls (I5), reports between-group voxelwise contrasts in stereotactic coordinates (x,y,z) comparing the overeating FTD group to controls and non-overeaters (I6), and provides whole-brain voxelwise VBM results (thresholded and corrected within an a priori ROI) with figures and coordinates (I7,I8). Full text includes background, methods, results, and discussion; fulltext_complete. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an rs-fMRI study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD with adequate sample sizes (41 bvFTD, 39 HC) and extensive network analyses. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (resting-state fMRI), I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample), I5 (≥6 patients and controls). However, the paper reports region-level (AAL parcellation) connectivity and MST-based graph metrics rather than voxelwise, whole-brain statistical contrasts reported in MNI/Talairach coordinates. Although images were registered to MNI space, no voxelwise between-group coordinate-based results are provided. Therefore it fails I6 and I7 and meets exclusion E6 (only ROI/region-based analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because, although it uses whole-brain VBM (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients within its symptomatic genetic groups (I4), and has adequate sample sizes (controls and patient subgroups exceed 6; I5), it does not report any between-group contrast in standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) that directly compares a clinically defined bvFTD group to healthy controls (I6 not met). The voxelwise whole-brain results presented are for gene-by-clinical-status groups (e.g., C9orf72/GRN/MAPT presymptomatic vs symptomatic vs controls), not for a bvFTD diagnostic group per se, so there are no clearly identified whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results coming specifically from a bvFTD target sample (I7 not met). No exclusion criteria were triggered. Therefore the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria for the bvFTD-focused meta-analysis and is excluded.

This paper is a study protocol/description of an ongoing observational cohort (LOF study). Exclusion criteria met: E8 (non-empirical/methods-only paper without original results). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET is included as an imaging modality in the protocol). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (participants are recruited based on late-onset frontal behavioral symptoms, not a clinically diagnosed bvFTD/Pick’s disease group), I5 (no reported bvFTD patient group size ≥6 is presented; the paper reports planned total cohort and expected FTD cases but no confirmed bvFTD group), I6 (no between-group voxelwise MNI/Talairach coordinates or contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls are reported), I7 (no reported group-level whole-brain voxelwise results). The manuscript lacks empirical group-level neuroimaging results required by the review (coordinates/voxelwise contrasts) and therefore must be excluded.

This is an empirical voxel-based morphometry (VBM) study that directly investigates cerebellar grey matter in bvFTD and related groups. It meets inclusion criteria: uses VBM (I3); includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants (n=23) (I4); has adequate sample sizes for bvFTD and controls (23 bvFTD, 16 controls) (I5); reports between-group contrasts of bvFTD versus controls registered to MNI space with voxelwise, whole-brain results (FWE-corrected) (I6, I7); and presents results in figures/text (I8). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria were triggered (not a review, not ROI-only, not seed-based FC/DTI/thickness-only, and no evidence of disqualifying comorbid sample characteristics).

The study uses FDG-PET and VBM and includes clinically-diagnosed bvFTD patients and adequate sample sizes, but the primary whole-brain voxel-wise analyses compare MAPT mutation carriers (a group combining symptomatic bvFTD and asymptomatic carriers) to non-carriers. The paper does not report a whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level contrast that is exclusively between a clinically-defined bvFTD (symptomatic) group and controls; voxelwise comparisons among symptomatic carriers alone were not performed due to small AC sample and group-level contrasts by diagnostic subgroup were limited to ROI/z-score analyses. Therefore it fails to meet inclusion criteria I6 and I7 requiring at least one between-group voxelwise contrast in standard (MNI/Talairach) space comparing a bvFTD group (not pooled with other patient groups) to controls. Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I5, I8. Inclusion criteria not met: I6, I7. No exclusion criteria were triggered.

This study is excluded because it does not provide a whole-brain, group-level voxel-based morphometry (VBM) contrast comparing a clinically defined bvFTD group to healthy controls with stereotactic coordinates. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses VBM), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD and Pick's disease cases), and I5 (sufficient overall MRI sample sizes: 42 patients, 35 controls). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no between-group contrast reported specifically for a bvFTD clinical group versus controls in MNI/Talairach space — VBM results are presented by pathological subgroups, not bvFTD syndromic group) and I7 (no whole-brain group-level result clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD target sample). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) were triggered. The provided full text appears complete.

Although the study includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients (behavioral-variant cases) and uses FDG-PET in a subset, it does not meet key imaging meta-analysis requirements. The paper presents descriptive imaging of a very small number of TBK1 carriers (FDG-PET in 2 patients; only five behavioral-variant FTD cases overall), and does not report any group-level, whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts in MNI/Talairach space comparing bvFTD to healthy controls. There is no voxelwise statistical comparison or coordinate table for a bvFTD vs control contrast, nor a sufficiently large bvFTD patient group for meta-analytic inclusion. Therefore it fails I5 (sample size), I6 (between-group voxelwise contrast), and I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group result). Exclusion criterion E6 applies because the study provides no whole-brain voxelwise results (only individual/descriptive imaging findings). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET used) and I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients). Inclusion criteria not met: I5, I6, I7. Full text is complete.

The study uses voxel-based morphometry (SPM12) so it meets I3. However, it does not include a clinically diagnosed bvFTD (behavioral variant FTD) or Pick’s disease patient group as the target sample (I4 not met). Therefore there is no bvFTD vs control between-group contrast reported (I6 not met) and no whole-brain result specific to a bvFTD sample (I7 not met). The bvFTD-specific sample-size requirement (I5) is not applicable/satisfied because no bvFTD group is reported. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Conclusion: EXCLUDED because it does not address the target clinical group (bvFTD/Pick’s disease) and thus fails I4, I5 (for target group), I6, and I7, despite meeting I3.

This is an autopsy/case-series report of five symptomatic VT (vacuolar tauopathy) patients (plus two presymptomatic carriers). While the study includes FDG‑PET and other imaging in individual cases (satisfying I3) and the sample includes clinically diagnosed FTD cases with behavioral features (satisfying I4), it does not meet several mandatory inclusion criteria: I5 (patient group size >=6) is not met — only five symptomatic cases; I6 is not met — no between‑group contrast comparing a bvFTD group to controls reported in MNI/Talairach space; I7 is not met — no group‑level whole‑brain (voxelwise) results from the target sample. The paper presents descriptive, individual-level imaging and neuropathology rather than voxelwise group analyses or statistical contrasts vs controls. Full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria from the provided list directly apply.

Although this study uses resting-state fMRI (I3) and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (18 bvFTD cases; I4) with adequate patient group size (n=32; I5), and reports voxelwise coordinates/cluster results (I8), it does NOT report any between-group voxelwise contrasts in MNI/Talairach space comparing a bvFTD group to healthy controls (i.e., no bvFTD-specific group vs control whole-brain contrast). The reported analyses are correlational (Reserve Index vs connectivity) within a mixed FTD sample and GRN+/- subgroups, and difference-of-slope comparisons between genetic subgroups, rather than a bvFTD vs control whole-brain contrast. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I6 and I7. Full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria from the list apply.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3), included a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=22) (I4) and healthy controls (n=38) with sample sizes ≥6 (I5), reports between-group voxelwise contrasts comparing bvFTD to controls with results localized in MNI space (I6), and provides whole-brain voxelwise VBM results identified as coming from the bvFTD group (I7). Results and coordinates are reported in main text and supplementary material (I8). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

EXCLUDED because the study does not report a whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrast specifically comparing bvFTD patients (not pooled with other patient groups) to healthy controls. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (used VBM), I4 (included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients among the sample), I5 (sufficient sample sizes overall and per group appear >6), and I8 (whole-brain results are reported in figures/tables). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no reported between-group contrast in MNI/Talairach space directly comparing bvFTD group to controls without pooling across diagnoses) and I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD target group). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it does not use any of the eligible imaging modalities (I3). It uses diffusion tensor imaging (DTI), arterial spin labeling (ASL) perfusion, and structural MRI (GM volume), not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample present; n=9) and I5 (patient and control groups ≥6). The paper also reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses (TBSS) comparing bvFTD with controls, satisfying I7. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (required imaging modality) and I6 (study does not clearly report between-group results in a defined stereotactic coordinate space [MNI/Talairach] in the provided text; no coordinate table or coordinates are present).
